ceramic.title: Bausch + Lomb Corporation (BLCO) Stock Analysis & Key Metrics (2025)
ceramic.snippet:
Bausch + Lomb operates a diversified business model centered on eye health, organized into three main segments. The Vision Care segment includes contact lenses (like the  Biotrue and  ULTRA brands) and lens care solutions. The Surgical segment provides a range of products for eye surgeries, such as intraocular lenses (IOLs) for cataract procedures and the  Stellaris surgical equipment. Finally, the Ophthalmic Pharmaceuticals segment develops and sells prescription medications for various eye conditions, including its recently launched dry-eye drug,  MIEBO . The company generates revenue by selling these products to a global network of eye care professionals, hospitals, distributors, and retailers.

 Bausch + Lombs financial statements paint a picture of a company with a solid market presence but severe underlying financial strain. On the income statement, revenue is growing at a healthy single-digit pace, reaching  $1.28 billion in the most recent quarter. Gross margins are also strong, consistently staying around the  60% mark. However, these positives are erased by high operating expenses.

  The primary growth drivers for Bausch + Lomb are centered on its product pipeline and operational improvements. The recent launch of MIEBO, a novel treatment for dry eye disease, represents a significant revenue opportunity in a large and underserved market. In its core Vision Care segment, growth is dependent on the continued rollout of its silicone hydrogel (SiHy) daily disposable lenses, such as INFUSE and ULTRA, to compete more effectively with Alcon and Cooper. The Surgical segment relies on innovation in intraocular lenses (IOLs) for cataract patients. Beyond revenue, a critical driver for earnings growth is margin expansion. The company is focused on streamlining its manufacturing footprint and supply chain to improve its operating margin, which currently lags well behind industry leaders.

 Bausch Health Companies Inc. (BHC) is a specialty pharmaceutical company with a diverse portfolio of products, but its business model is dominated by its high-margin, patent-protected drugs. The company is structured into several key segments: Salix, which focuses on gastrointestinal (GI) treatments and is the companys crown jewel, featuring the blockbuster drug Xifaxan; an International segment with a mix of branded and generic drugs sold outside the U.S.; Solta Medical, an aesthetics device business; and a Diversified Products segment that includes older drugs and some over-the-counter (OTC) products. BHC generates revenue primarily through the sale of these prescription and OTC products to wholesalers, distributors, and directly to healthcare providers. Its customer base is broad, but its revenue is highly concentrated on a few key products.
